        "Issue": "Only one bridge governor on L2",
        "Severity": "Medium",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "On `L2` bridge may have only one governor that is set during initialization and can't be changed later. Such design puts lot of responsibility on one address. Some of most severe bridge exploits involve private key compromising. If one governor address gets compromised the whole bridge is put on risk.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider adding more bridge governors on `L2`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Transaction Ordering Dependence for `initialize()` Functions",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "The various `initialize()` functions of upgradeable contracts are not constructors. There\u00e2\u20ac\u2122s a chance that someone can call these after the contracts have been deployed but before the development team calls them. Consequently, contracts may be initialized with values not expected by the development team.",
        "Recommendation": "Be aware of this issue, and be prepared to redeploy your contracts if these calls are front-run. Do not use your project until you have checked that your calls to these functions went through.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Different behavior on governance initialization in Proxy",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "Governance initialization differs between layers. On `L1` it is initialized with `initGovernance(...)` in the Proxy's constructor, but on `L2` funcion `init_governance(...)` is implicitly imported and must be externaly called outside the constructor.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider unifying implementation of governance initialization across the layers and moving `init_governance(...)` function into an Proxy's constructor on `L2`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Different behavior in governance candidates proposal",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "Governance candidates proposal mechanisms differ between layers. On `L1` only one pending candidate may be proposed, but on `L2` multiple candidates may be proposed and accepting proposal does not relay on proposing order. Such difference may result in confusion and potentially lead to unwanted scenario.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider unifying the governance candidate proposal mechanism across the layers.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Missing invariant check in function `initGovernance()`",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/components/Governance.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `initGovernance()` does not check if the number of governors is zero. Since the governor has an important role, we recommend to ensure that this invariant is true. The code is reproduced below.\n\n```solidity=\nfunction initGovernance() internal {\n    GovernanceInfoStruct storage gub = getGovernanceInfo();\n    require(!gub.initialized, "ALREADY_INITIALIZED");\n    gub.initialized = true;\n\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit-issue Invariant not checked. This function must ensure that \n    //              the list of governors has zero length.\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n\n    // Add the initial governer.\n    acceptNewGovernor(msg.sender);\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Ensure that there are no governors already set.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Do not trust in function `isContract(...)`",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/libraries/Addresses.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `isContract(...)` attempts to identify if the external entity is a contract or an EOA. It is unsafe to assume that an address for which this function returns `false` is an externally-owned account (EOA) and not a contract, and the development team is aware of this situation.\n\n```solidity=\nfunction isContract(address account) internal view returns (bool) {\n    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit-note Do not trust in this function when it returns\n    //             "false".\n    ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    uint256 size;\n    assembly {\n        size := extcodesize(account)\n    }\n    return size > 0;\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Always assume that you are dealing with an external contract. Never trust this function when it returns `false`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "External proxy governance initialization",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "On `L2` proxy governance is initialized with external function `init_governance(...)` that must be called outside of constructor. This may add unnecessary complexity for proxy contract deployemnt. Additionaly on `L1` proxy governance is initialized in constructor. Such differences between initializtion of proxies across the layers may lead to confusion and unintended misconfiguration at deployemnt time.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider unifying implementation of governance initialization across the layers by moving `init_governance(...)` function into an Proxy's constructor on `L2`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Removing governor is easier than adding one",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "Currently governance managment mechanisms (L1: proxy, bridge; L2: proxy) consist of two-step process for adding governor, and only one-step process for removing governor. Some of most severe bridge exploits involve private key compromising. If one governor address gets compromised the rest of governors may be put at risk.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider securing the governor removal process.",
    },

        "Issue": "Added implementation time delay value may be overwritten",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "The functions `addImplementation(...)` (`L1`) and `add_implementation(...)` (`L2`) are used to add new implementation. The hash of new implementation code (with data and `finalize` flag) is a key to time delay value. After this time new implementation may be used as the logic for the proxy contract. Currently it is possible to overwrite the time delay value by adding the implementation that was already added. This may lead to dangerous scenario where changing implementation may be postponed.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider checking if implementation was already added to avoid overwriting the time delay value.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Not validating the implementation contract",
        "Severity": "Low",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/upgrade/Proxy.sol"],
        "Description": "The proxy pattern requires that memory layouts stay consistent between contract and compiler upgrades. No existing tool can verify that an upgrade is safe against a compromise. If the destination of `delegatecall` has no code, then the call will successfully return. If the proxy is set incorrectly, or if the destination was destroyed, any call to the proxy will succeed but will not send back data. Ideally, the proxy must ensure that the implementation address is correct. However, this protocol only ensures that the implementation address is different from `address(0x0)`. This is a weak check and is not able to catch human errors when typing the address of the new implementation contract.",
        "Recommendation": "In order to ensure that the proxy is really pointing to the proper implementation, the implementation can implement a function that returns some pass code. The very first call to the implementation will retrieve this password (i.e., version). If the password matches, the implementation is acknowledged. Otherwise, the implementation address is set to `address(0x0)`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Function `implementationIsFrozen(...)` returns `false` when no implementation is set",
        "Severity": "Undetermined",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/upgrade/Proxy.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `implementationIsFrozen(...)` is returning `false` when the `_implementation` has not being set yet. The code comments are not clear about the reason for this. Instead of only returning `true` and `false`, the function can return one out of the three possible states: `frozen`, `not-frozen`, `implementation-not-set`. The code is reproduced below.\n\n```solidity=\nfunction implementationIsFrozen() private returns (bool) {\n    address _implementation = implementation();\n\n    ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit Function is returning that the implementation is \n    //        not frozen when we do not have an implementation set\n    //        A better practice would be to have three possible outputs,\n    //        instead of only two: (frozen, not-frozen, implementation-not-set)\n    ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    if (_implementation == address(0x0)) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    (bool success, bytes memory returndata) = _implementation.delegatecall(\n        abi.encodeWithSignature("isFrozen()")\n    );\n    require(success, string(returndata));\n    return abi.decode(returndata, (bool));\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Improve the function for returning the three possible states of the implementation: a) `frozen`; b) `not-frozen`; c) `implementation-not-set`. Review the code for all the calls for this function and update accordingly.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Different behavior on removing implementation in Proxy",
        "Severity": "Info",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": 'Reaction on removing implementation that was not added differs between layers. On `L1` removing implementation that was not added results in error. Described code is reproduces below:\n```solidity=\nrequire(activationTime > 0, "UNKNOWN_UPGRADE_INFORMATION");\n```\nHowever on `L2` such action results in quiet success.\n\n```cairo=\n// Quiet success if activation time is 0 (i.e. not added).\nif (time == 0) {\n    return ();\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Consider unifying implementation of removal functionality across the layers.",
    },

        "Description": "Functions in `NamedStorage` library are taking `string memory tag_` argument. Since the `tag_` is not modified, passing this variable as a `calldata` would save gas when calling functions from `NamedStorage` library.",

        "Description": "Governance mechanisms differ between layers:\n- **L1 Bridge:** `L1` bridge may have multiple governors. Governors can be proposed, added and removed.\n- **L2 Bridge:** `L2` bridge may have only one governor that is set during initialization and can't be changed later.\n- **L1 Proxy:** `L1` proxy may have one pending candidate\n- **L2 Proxy:** On `L2` proxy multiple candidates may be proposed and accepting proposal does not relay on proposing order\n\nSuch difference may result in confusion and potentially lead to unwanted scenario.",

        "Issue": "Governance Model invariants are not checked",
        "Severity": "Info",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/components/Governance.sol"],
        "Description": "The Governance Model is based on a mapping holding all the governors. The model does not track the number of governors, and so it is not possible to check for broken invariants. For instance, during initialization, the Governance should have zero governors. When adding a new governor, the number of governors should be increased by one. When removing a governor, the number of governors should be decreased by one. The ability to list the Governors can be particularly important when upgrading the contract. The [Enumerable Map](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/3.x/api/utils#EnumerableMap) seems to be a more appropriate data structure for the Governance model.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider using the Enumerable Map data structure for the governance model and ensure that invariants hold after each operation.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Arbitrary fees are accepted in function `StarknetEthBridge.deposit(...)`",
        "Severity": "Info",
        "Contracts": [
            "src/starkware/starknet/apps/starkgate/eth/StarknetEthBridge.sol"
        ],
        "Description": 'Function `StarknetEthBridge.deposit(...)` receives an `amount` to be deposited into the `l2Recipient` (layer 2 address). The function only checks if `msg.value` is enough to cover `amount`. The remaining value is considered as `fee`. The `fee` is not validated, so it can be zero. In case the user makes a mistake and passes a low value as `amount` and a large number as `msg.value`, the difference `msg.value - amount` will be credit as `fee` paid by the user. The code is reproduced below.\n\n\n```solidity=\nfunction deposit(uint256 amount, uint256 l2Recipient) public payable override {\n    // Make sure msg.value is enough to cover amount. The remaining value is fee.\n    require(msg.value >= amount, "INSUFFICIENT_VALUE");\n    ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit "fee" is not checked for any reasonable interval\n    ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    uint256 fee = msg.value - amount;\n    require(address(this).balance - fee <= maxTotalBalance(), "MAX_BALANCE_EXCEEDED");\n    sendMessage(amount, l2Recipient, fee);\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Design some scheme or solution to prevent users from spending more funds than necessary. Revert when the `fee` is not appropriate.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Charging fee for zero deposits",
        "Severity": "Info",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/starknet/apps/starkgate/eth/Transfers.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `Transfers.transferIn(...)` receive the `token address`, the `sender`, and the `amount` to be deposited. When `amount` equals zero, this function does not revert the transaction. Thus, the caller function `StarknetERC20Bridge.deposit(...)` charges the `fee` passed in `msg.value`. A better approach would be to revert the transaction and not charge the `fee` for zero transfers. The functions `StarknetERC20Bridge.deposit(...)` and `Transfers.transferIn(...)` are reproduced below with audit comments.\n\n\n```solidity=\nfunction StarknetERC20Bridge.deposit(uint256 amount, uint256 l2Recipient) public payable override {\n    /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit-issue Function does not revert when "amount" is zero\n    /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    require(msg.value >= amount, "INSUFFICIENT_VALUE");\n    uint256 fee = msg.value - amount;\n    require(address(this).balance - fee <= maxTotalBalance(), "MAX_BALANCE_EXCEEDED");\n    sendMessage(amount, l2Recipient, fee);\n}\n```\n\n```solidity=\nfunction Transfers.transferIn( address token, address sender, \n                              uint256 amount ) internal {\n    /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    // @audit-issue Not reverting the transaction when "amount" is zero \n    /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n    if (amount == 0) return;\n    IERC20 erc20Token = IERC20(token);\n    uint256 bridgeBalanceBefore = erc20Token.balanceOf(address(this));\n    uint256 expectedAfter = bridgeBalanceBefore + amount;\n    require(expectedAfter >= bridgeBalanceBefore, "OVERFLOW");\n\n    bytes memory callData = abi.encodeWithSelector(\n        erc20Token.transferFrom.selector,\n        sender,\n        address(this),\n        amount\n    );\n    token.safeTokenContractCall(callData);\n\n    uint256 bridgeBalanceAfter = erc20Token.balanceOf(address(this));\n    require(bridgeBalanceAfter == expectedAfter, "INCORRECT_AMOUNT_TRANSFERRED");\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Do not charge `fee` for null transactions. Revert the transaction when `amount` is zero.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Unlocked Pragma",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "The contracts use the caret for specifying the Solidity version. The compiler will use the specified version and above.",
        "Recommendation": "Lock the contracts to a specific Solidity version.",
    },

        "Issue": "Old Solidity version",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "Currently all Solidity files are in version `^0.6.12`. It is recommended to use newer Solidity version, to avoid known bugs from previous versions, and utilize new features added with new version.",
        "Recommendation": "Consider changing Solidity version to `0.8.*`.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Known bugs for Solidity `0.6.12`",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/*"],
        "Description": "Currently used Solidity version is `0.6.12`. Using older version of Solidity requires awarness of [known bugs](https://github.com/ethereum/solidity/blob/84cdcec2cfb1fe9d4a9171d3ed0ffefd6107ee42/docs/bugs_by_version.json#L1451).",
        "Recommendation": "Currently no compiler bugs are in direct harm for the protocol. However, to mitigate issues in further development, make sure that known `0.6.12` bugs do not affect the protocol, and consider following some sugestions listed below:\n- do not place statically-sized calldata after the dynamically-sized argument when defining a function inputs ([Head Overflow Bug in Calldata Tuple ABI-Reencoding](https://blog.soliditylang.org/2022/08/08/calldata-tuple-reencoding-head-overflow-bug/))\n- make sure that overriding functions do not change the data location of parameters from memory to calldata\n- make sure that `abi.decode(...)` on `memory` data do not allow for malicious behavior (crafting input that reads memory data outside given location)\n- do not use keccak hash function in inline assembly.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Gas optimization in `ERC20.sol` `transferFrom(...)` function",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/tokens/ERC20/ERC20.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `transferFrom(...)` will call `_transfer(...)` and `_approve(...)` function. Both two functions do the zero address checks, which is duplicated and wasting gas. Similarly for `_burnFrom(...)` function.\n\nCheck in function `_transfer(...)`\n```solidity\nrequire(sender != address(0), "ERC20: transfer from the zero address");\nrequire(recipient != address(0), "ERC20: transfer to the zero address");\n```\nAnd in function `_approve(...)` \n```solidity\nrequire(owner != address(0), "ERC20: approve from the zero address");\nrequire(spender != address(0), "ERC20: approve to the zero address");\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Consider checking the zero address in the `transferFrom(...)` function to save gas.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Constant is never used",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/upgrade/StorageSlots.sol"],
        "Description": "The constant `CALL_PROXY_IMPL_SLOT` in `StorageSlots` contract is never used. This constant represents the storage slot with the address of the call-proxy current implementation.",
        "Recommendation": "Remove the unused constant.",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "The usage of `abi.encodeWithSelector(...)` should be avoided",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/starkware/solidity/upgrade/Proxy.sol"],
        "Description": "The function `upgradeTo(...)` in the contract `Proxy` uses `abi.encodeWithSelector`. However, the compiler does not check whether the provided value matches the expected type by the called function (in this case `initialize(...)`). In version 0.8.11 was added `abi.encodeCall` to perform type checking during compile time. \n\n```solidity=\nfunction upgradeTo(\n        address newImplementation,\n        bytes calldata data,\n        bool finalize\n    ) external payable onlyGovernance notFinalized notFrozen {\n        \n        ...\n        setImplementation(newImplementation);\n        \n        // NOLINTNEXTLINE: low-level-calls controlled-delegatecall.\n        (bool success, bytes memory returndata) = newImplementation\n            .delegatecall(\n                abi.encodeWithSelector(this.initialize.selector, data)\n            );\n        require(success, string(returndata));\n        ...\n    }\n```",
        "Recommendation": "Replace `abi.encodeWithSelector(...)` by `abi.encodeCall` as safer way to perform ABI-encoding. Consider bumping Solidity pragma even if breaking change occurs. For more details: https://blog.soliditylang.org/2021/12/20/solidity-0.8.11-release-announcement/",
    },
    {
        "Issue": "Gas Optimization in `_acceptGovernance(...)`",
        "Severity": "Best Practices",
        "Contracts": ["src/starkware/solidity/components/Governance.sol"],
        "Description": 'The function `_acceptGovernance(...)` loads `gub.candidateGovernor` from storage twice. However, we can replace it by `msg.sender` on the second time to save about `100` gas.\n\n```solidity=\nfunction _acceptGovernance() internal {\n    // The new governor was proposed as a candidate by the current governor.\n    GovernanceInfoStruct storage gub = getGovernanceInfo();\n    require(msg.sender == gub.candidateGovernor, "ONLY_CANDIDATE_GOVERNOR");\n\n    // Update state.\n    // @audit-issue Gas optimization by using msg.sender\n    acceptNewGovernor(gub.candidateGovernor);\n    gub.candidateGovernor = address(0x0);\n}\n```',
        "Recommendation": "Consider using `msg.sender` instead of `gub.candidateGovernor` to save gas.\n```diff=\n-    acceptNewGovernor(gub.candidateGovernor);\n+    acceptNewGovernor(msg.sender);\n```",
    },
